description: Pipeline plugin hooks. Every command routes through `hooks/run-hook.sh`, which resolves an absolute `pipeline` binary (PATH → $BUN_INSTALL/bin → ~/.bun/bin → /opt/homebrew/bin → /usr/local/bin) and execs `pipeline hook <name>` — Claude Code runs hooks through a non-interactive /bin/sh that never sources ~/.zshrc, so a Dock- or Start-menu-launched session cannot otherwise see a global install. THE RELAYS ARE CLI SUBCOMMANDS, NOT FILES IN THIS PLUGIN (plugin-thin p6): they live in `IvanMurzak/pipeline` as `src/hooks/*.ts`, so a hook's version is the installed CLI's version by construction. This plugin therefore REQUIRES `@baizor/pipeline` — `bun add -g @baizor/pipeline` — and the --loud SessionStart entry below is what says so when it is missing. Registrations: Stop → analytics relay (token usage from transcript) then stats relay (token + tool-failure enrichment for .pipeline/.stats/); SubagentStop (matcher: pipeline-manager) → analytics relay (manager.stopped liveness signal when a pipeline-manager subagent ends — the matcher keeps the hook from spawning for every other subagent) then stats relay; Notification → analytics relay (run.awaiting_input when a permission prompt or an input request blocks the session); SessionStart → the session relay (appends one session.opened line to the project's .runtime/events.jsonl and nothing else — this is what is left of the deleted local dashboard's launcher hook, kept because the journal is ux-v2's telemetry source and `pipeline logs` renders the event), THEN the department notifier relay (department-mesh task a1: ensures the `pipeline department notify` background daemon is running detached and drains its pending-notification journal into SessionStart additionalContext — a department task that reaches INPUT_REQUIRED/AUTH_REQUIRED or a terminal state announces itself even across sessions, gated by its own switch PIPELINE_DEPARTMENT_NOTIFY_ENABLED (falling back to the deprecated PIPELINE_MESH_NOTIFY_ENABLED with a warning), default ON, no-op until `pipeline cloud connect` has been run once); PreToolUse → analytics relay (live mirror binding + run-level bypass START synthesis for pipeline-manager spawns); PostToolUse → analytics relay (tool counts + agent spawns + bypass END/fallback lifecycle synthesis); UserPromptSubmit → prompt match relay (BM25-matches the submitted prompt against the project's PIPELINE.md manifests and, on a confident single match only, injects one line of additionalContext suggesting the pipeline — gated by its own opt-in switch PIPELINE_PROMPT_MATCH_ENABLED, off by default). The whole journal/analytics system is ON BY DEFAULT — every journal hook runs at entry unless PIPELINE_JOURNAL_ENABLED is explicitly opted out with a falsy value 0/false/no/off (the master opt-OUT switch; the prompt match relay is a separate OPT-IN gated by PIPELINE_PROMPT_MATCH_ENABLED instead, off by default) — and is additionally a no-op when cwd has no .pipeline/ (the department notifier relay is independent of this project-scoped gate — department tasks are org-scoped, not project-scoped, so it runs the same in every directory, gated only by PIPELINE_DEPARTMENT_NOTIFY_ENABLED). EXCEPTION: Stop and SubagentStop additionally run the stats relay (token + tool-failure enrichment for the per-run measurement files under .pipeline/.stats/, via the shared backfillProject core), which is ON BY DEFAULT and gated by its own PIPELINE_STATS_ENABLED (set 0 to disable); it too no-ops when the project has no .stats dir. SECOND EXCEPTION: the Notification branch is evaluated BEFORE the PIPELINE_JOURNAL_ENABLED opt-out and carries its own gate PIPELINE_AWAITING_INPUT_ENABLED (default ON, set 0 to disable) — a blocked run is worth surfacing through `pipeline logs` even for a user who is not connected to the cloud dashboard.
